markup:
For watching sports during the daytime, the **brightest-looking projector screen is usually a high-gain Ambient Light Rejecting (ALR) screen**, especially if you're using it in a bright living room.

However, the best screen depends on whether you're watching indoors with sunlight coming through windows or outdoors in direct sunlight.

## Best screen types for daytime sports

| Screen type | Typical gain | Daytime performance |
|---|---:|---|
| High-gain ALR screen | 1.2–2.0+ | Excellent with compatible projector and lighting |
| Fresnel ALR screen for UST projectors | 0.8–1.5 | Excellent indoors |
| Standard white screen | 1.0–1.3 | Fair in bright rooms |
| Matte gray screen | 0.6–0.9 | Fair; better blacks, dimmer whites |
| Standard outdoor screen | 1.0 | Poor in direct sunlight |

**Important:** Higher gain doesn't always mean a better image. ALR screens reject light from certain directions, so the projector's position and the direction of sunlight matter enormously.
